content.comment_body: I'm searching for a way to automate temperature control in a room. My setup uses a frequency drive with a 0-10V input. The fan should run constantly at 10Hz in standard mode (between 0 and 16 degrees). If the temperature exceeds 16 degrees, the fan speed should increase by 5Hz per degree up to a maximum of 50Hz. Although I have researched similar scenarios, I haven't found a suitable solution yet, as it's my first time needing both analog inputs and outputs.

This requirement is quite unique. Typically, ready-made solutions for such applications are uncommon, but I'll tackle your problem and develop a proposed solution. By the way, which [product_name] module are you planning to use?
Here's one possible approach: The fan runs at 10Hz up to 16°C, then, for each degree increase, raises speed by 5Hz. Since you didn't specify the [product_name], I set the hardware to [article_no].

Thank you for the quick reply—I'd never have found that program myself. I’ll check which [product_name] modules I currently have; perhaps it’s [article_no], but I'll let you know if I don’t find [article_no]. Is it possible to adjust the set temperature directly via the display and buttons instead of updating the program each time?

The program can be adapted to work with a [article_no] as well, but not with [article_no], since it doesn’t feature analog MUX. If you want to modify limits through the display, you’ll need a custom message for each threshold. To allow adjustments via buttons, you'd have to implement 15 setpoint options.

Great solution you've created! One note: If your PT100 sensor's wire breaks, the measured value will drop, and you may want the fan to run at maximum speed in that case. Ultimately, your process should determine the best response. Kind Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring how to automate exhaust fan speed based on temperature readings, with automatic analog speed adjustments handled by [product_name] modules. There's some uncertainty about hardware selection—mainly regarding analog I/O capabilities—and about how to let users change temperature setpoints directly via the unit’s display, rather than altering the program. Additionally, there are discussions on improving fault tolerance by accounting for sensor errors in the logic.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a practical, programmable solution for analog fan control, with the ability to adjust temperature limits directly from the display or buttons. They aim to avoid regular software changes and also expect robust handling of sensor faults.
